prs.title: Remove legacy localization handbacks
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body: OneLoc now supplies translations from its localization package. The checked-in LCL handbacks are no longer used by the update pipeline.

prs.title: Fix idle cache clean timer never being stored on Session
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
`scheduleIdleCacheClean` created a timer via `time.AfterFunc` but never assigned it to `s.idleCacheCleanTimer`, only using the local variable for self-identity comparison inside the timer's own callback. As a result, `cancelIdleCacheClean` (called from `Close`) could never find an active timer to stop, so `Close` always blocked until the full 30 second idle delay elapsed and the timer fired naturally, even when no cleanup was actually pending.

This was discovered while debugging unexpectedly slow `Close` calls in a test exercising real session watch/close behavior.

prs.title: Restart a file's imports when a later arrival lowers its node_modules depth
prs.author: cplieger
prs.body:
When the files parser reaches a file again at a lower depth, it lowers `lowestDepth` and sets `startSubtasks`, but the `startedSubTasks` guard skips the restart because the first arrival already started the file's imports. Those imports keep the first arrival's depth, so a file reached through `node_modules` first and then from a root file without passing through `node_modules` leaves its own imports in `sourceFilesFoundSearchingNodeModules`, and which arrival comes first depends on scheduling.

**Impact:** in a monorepo where a package is reached both by a relative import and through a `node_modules` link, which files count as library files changes between identical runs. The same build can then emit different files (#64498), and an analyzer on the API gives a different answer each run: on vitest, 20 opens of one configuration gave five different counts.

The change restarts the subtasks whenever the depth drops, even when they were already started. Each restart strictly lowers a file's `lowestDepth`, so the extra work is bounded.

The compiler test `symlinkedPackageReachedRelativelyIsNotExternalLibrary` has `a.ts` import `./lib/index` and `b.ts` import `lib` through a `node_modules` symlink to `lib/`. Without the change, `lib/util.ts` counts as from an external library and its `util.js` is missing from the emit baseline.

prs.title: Fix flaky diagnostic on JS constructor-defined properties
prs.author: weswigham
prs.body:
Fixes a flaky diagnostic reported in the server logs. Only some checker entrypoints would trigger `getTypeOfSymbol` on constructor-declared properties (implicit any errors from widening the auto type), making the diagnostic depend on if emit had occurred already using a given checker or not.

Now we always check them. (Previously, sometimes only their flow type would be calculated - diagnostics wouldn't be issued.)

prs.title: [api] Stop dropping dispose Promises in the async API
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
A few objects in the async API accidentally used `[Symbol.dispose]()` instead of `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`, throwing their disposal Promise away. I think that should be up to the consumer whether to fire and forget.

The second commit improves our own diagnostic message when you use a `using` on an AsyncDisposable, suggesting you use `await using` instead.

prs.title: Update DOM types
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
- **New APIs:** Web Serial (`navigator.serial`, including worker support), Document Picture-in-Picture (`documentPictureInPicture`), `CloseWatcher`, and `Origin`.
- **HTML sanitization:** Adds `Element.setHTML()`, sanitizer options for `setHTMLUnsafe()` and `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe()`, and processing-instruction configuration.
- **WebGPU:** Adds `"webgpu"` canvas context overloads, global usage/flag constants, additional device limits, pipeline-layout `immediateSize`, and the `"snorm10-10-10-2"` vertex format.
- **WebTransport:** Adds connection/stream statistics, dedicated receive/send stream interfaces, and reliability/protocol properties.
- **CSS and animation:** Adds `CSSFontFaceDescriptors`, highlight hit-testing, container-condition information, `CSSStyleValue` support in keyframes, and animation references on animation/transition events.
- **Other additions:** Brotli compression, `HTMLMediaElement.captureStream()`, `VisualViewport` scroll-end events, fullscreen keyboard-lock options, and resource-timing content/delivery types.
- **Potential compatibility changes:** `WritableStreamDefaultWriter.write()` and `TransformStreamDefaultController.enqueue()` now require a chunk argument; several SVG geometry APIs use `SVGPoint`, `SVGRect`, and `SVGMatrix` instead of their `DOM*` counterparts; `SVGFilterElement` no longer inherits `SVGURIReference`; and `HTMLImageElement.crossOrigin` is narrowed to `"anonymous" | "use-credentials" | null`.

prs.title: [api] Report project reference diagnostics on programs without a config file
prs.author: cplieger
prs.body:
* [ ] There is an associated issue in the `Backlog` milestone (**required**)
* [x] Code is up-to-date with the `main` branch
* [x] You've successfully run `npx hereby test`
* [x] You've successfully run `npx hereby lint`
* [x] You've successfully run `npx hereby check:format`
* [x] There are new or updated tests validating the change

Fixes #64629

A program created through `createPrograms` has no configuration file, so its `ParsedCommandLine.ConfigFile` is nil. Any project reference diagnostic on such a program crashes the API server with a nil pointer dereference in `CreateDiagnosticAtReferenceSyntax`.

**Impact:** a tool that builds its own program for a repository that references a non-composite project kills the whole API server process, losing every open snapshot, and the tool sees only an EOF. That is an ordinary monorepo setup, where `tsc -p` reports TS6306 and keeps going, so an analyzer on the API stops on that repository instead of analyzing it.

`CreateDiagnosticAtReferenceSyntax` now returns nil when `ConfigFile` is nil, and its caller in `verifyProjectReferences` already falls back to a compiler diagnostic in that case.

`TestCreateProgramReportsNonCompositeProjectReference` creates such a program with a reference to a non-composite project and expects TS6306 as its only program diagnostic, and it panics without the fix.

I met this while building deadset-ts, the TypeScript analyzer of [deadset](https://github.com/cplieger/deadset), on the TypeScript 7 API. That
…(truncated)

prs.title: [api] Skip disk-layout import diagnostics for customized module resolutions
prs.author: cplieger
prs.body:
A resolution answered by a static `moduleResolutions` entry or a `resolveModuleName` callback never sets `ResolvedUsingTsExtension`, so under `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` a relative `./x.ts` value import it answers raises a false TS2876 where `tsc` reports none.

Following the review, customized resolutions now skip the checker diagnostics that rest on how the built-in resolver mapped the specifier onto disk, and `StaticModuleResolution` is unchanged from `main`. `ResolvedModule` gains an internal `IsCustomResolution`, set in `staticModuleResolutionToResolvedModule`, which static entries and callback results both go through and the built-in fallbacks never do. When it is set, the checker skips the [`ResolvedUsingTsExtension` block of `resolveExternalModule`](tsc/internal/checker/checker.go#L15523): TS2846, TS5097, TS2876, TS2877 and TS2878. Only TS2876 could fire for a customized resolution before, and the diagnostics outside that block still apply.

`TestCustomModuleResolutionsSkipUnsafeRewriteDiagnostic` resolves `./b.ts` through a static entry and `./c.ts` through the callback in one program and expects no semantic diagnostics. On `main` it reports two TS2876.

One related behavior is unchanged: emit still rewrites `./b.ts` to `./b.js` from the specifier text, and with this block skipped the checker no longer verifies that a customized target has the matching output path.
